title: Stacked Diamond Flow
prompt: Draw a directed artificial flow graph built from four stacked diamond gadgets. Start at s and end at t. For each k=0,1,2,3 create top node uk, bottom node vk, left branch ak, and right branch bk. Add directed edges uk->ak, uk->bk, ak->vk, bk->vk for every k. Chain them with s->u0, v0->u1, v1->u2, v2->u3, v3->t. Add cross-layer directed shortcuts a0->b1, b0->a1, a1->b2, b1->a2, a2->b3, b2->a3. Make layers vertical from left to right.

suggestions: Place each gadget in a consistent diamond: u_k on the top row, v_k on the bottom row, a_k on a middle-left row, and b_k on a middle-right row, with equal spacing across k=0..3.
Align the four u_k nodes on one horizontal row and the four v_k nodes on another, and align a_k/b_k pairs on a common middle row where possible.
Route the a_k->b_{k+1} shortcuts as upper or outward arcs and the b_k->a_{k+1} shortcuts as lower or opposite arcs so they do not pass through the interiors of adjacent diamonds.
Increase local separation around a1/b1 and a2/b2, or move the shortcut curves farther from those node labels.
Make the layered columns more uniform from left to right to reduce crossings and expose the repeated structure.
